nodes.label: Go Live-session Engine
nodes.rationale: Planned persona-agnostic runtime intended to own deterministic media, turn timing, and persistence while delegating only speech and reasoning to models; all 58 implementation tasks are unchecked in the plan.

nodes.label: Four-plane Architecture
nodes.rationale: Separates media, cognition, session, and persistence so latency-sensitive mechanics remain deterministic and model access stays narrow.

nodes.label: Per-session Actor
nodes.rationale: One owner goroutine holds all mutable state to avoid mutexes on the latency path and prevent competing writers.

nodes.label: Speaker
nodes.rationale: Realtime speech model always owns the mouth and phrasing but must stay inside the compiled persona directives.

nodes.label: Thinker
nodes.rationale: A speculative reasoning model supplies notes and assessments without authoring runtime beliefs or speaking directly.

nodes.label: Claims Ledger
nodes.rationale: Shared single-writer memory prevents long-range contradictions between the Speaker and Thinker.

nodes.label: Deterministic Pre-gate
nodes.rationale: Incremental lexicon matching on ASR partials should decide DEFER before end-of-turn, avoiding a blocking classifier call.

nodes.label: Pre-synthesized Stall Bank
nodes.rationale: Persona-voiced clips hide Thinker latency and must begin within 50 ms; voice seam quality remains an open spike.

nodes.label: Barge-in Draining and Heard-truth Truncation
nodes.rationale: Cancellation is insufficient unless downstream audio, timers, vendor history, transcript, and recording are reconciled to what the human actually heard.

nodes.label: Voice-to-voice Latency Budget
nodes.rationale: Targets roughly 540 ms p50 and 850 ms p95; vendor end-of-turn to first audio dominates and threatens the stated sub-800 ms target.

nodes.label: Realtime Backpressure Policy
nodes.rationale: Drops superseded/audio data under overload while preserving control, timers, and non-audio events; recording silence-fills instead of blocking media.

nodes.label: Async Ceiling Judge
nodes.rationale: Guarantees detection and labeling after speech but cannot prevent the original breach; an in-character walk-back is only best-effort repair.

nodes.label: Planned Engine Gaps
nodes.rationale: The design is comprehensive but implementation remains phased: real media, ASR, pre-gate, thinker, ledger, recording/S3, ingest, degradation, fidelity, soak, chaos, security, and deploy work are all planned rather than complete.

nodes.label: EngineContract v1.6
nodes.rationale: Frozen Python-compiled runtime slice; the engine pins major version, retains minor version, and must inject system_prompt verbatim.

nodes.label: Knowledge Ceiling
nodes.rationale: A persona answering above its ceiling invalidates comparability; prompt-only enforcement is explicitly insufficient under pressure.

nodes.label: Hidden Interviewer Scorecard
nodes.rationale: Ground-truth key is used only after the session and must never reach the realtime persona model.

nodes.label: RealtimeBroker
nodes.rationale: Mints sealed ephemeral configuration for a browser-to-vendor call; it is deliberately not a model invocation port.

nodes.label: Direct Browser-to-vendor Media
nodes.rationale: Avoids routing live audio through Python because that would add hundreds of milliseconds to a sub-second interaction budget.

nodes.label: Speaker-only Voice Limitation
nodes.rationale: Current voice path lets one realtime model decide both knowledge and speech; no Thinker, claims ledger, deterministic pre-gate, belief injection, or post-hoc ceiling enforcement exists in the live path.

nodes.label: Gemini Session Resumption
nodes.source_location: § Surviving the session cap and reconnects

nodes.label: Browser Session Recording
nodes.rationale: Browser is the only component currently holding both live audio sides because no media flows through engined.

nodes.label: Engine Recording Producer Seam
nodes.rationale: producer=engine preserves the same downstream recording identity once the future engine recorder is wired.

nodes.label: Recording Security and Retention Gap
nodes.source_location: § Consent, retention, and where the bytes land
nodes.rationale: Recordings, including named employees' video, are retained indefinitely with manual deletion; the API has no auth and no purge job or lifecycle rule.

nodes.label: Server-stamped Session Transcript
nodes.source_location: §§ Why the clock is server-side; modality
nodes.rationale: Text and voice normalize into one evidence shape with server-owned ordering and timestamps.

nodes.label: Missing Voice Timing Telemetry
nodes.rationale: WPM, interruptions, silence handling, and filler density are not extracted in current voice sessions; reports must say not measurable instead of emitting fake zeroes.

nodes.label: Control-plane Storage Boundary Leak
nodes.rationale: get_repo initializes a SQLite connection per request; production should use a connection-pool dependency.

nodes.label: Current Spoken Practice Path
nodes.rationale: Portal currently bypasses the production Go/Rust engine and connects directly to Gemini/OpenAI.

nodes.label: Provider Credential Operational Blocker
nodes.rationale: Spoken session and live typed-session walkthroughs were not verified because the configured Gemini key returned API_KEY_INVALID and dependent calls surfaced as 502.

nodes.label: Unverified End-to-end Browser Walkthrough
nodes.rationale: Real camera/mic prompts, call continuity, video seek, tab close, launcher dedupe, and long-call A/V lip sync still require manual browser verification.

nodes.label: Deterministic Report Engine
nodes.rationale: Standalone bundle-in/report-out design; scoring numbers belong to code while one optional judge call supplies evidence-bound prose.

nodes.label: Multilingual Scoring Validity Gap
nodes.rationale: English pattern detectors under-measure Hindi/Hinglish/Urdu interviews; current design scores with per-criterion low-confidence warnings unless the operator enables refusal.

nodes.label: Persona-cohort Calibration
nodes.rationale: Genuine manager comparability requires about 50 sessions per archetype and strictly version-matched cohorts; cold-start cut points are only calibration judgments.

nodes.label: Realtime Call Cost Dominance
nodes.rationale: A 20-minute voice session is estimated near $1.07, with the live call around $0.85; model selection and session length dominate savings.

nodes.label: Text-first Bridge
nodes.rationale: Text chat was deliberately built first to produce the transcript/evaluation artifact while the sub-800 ms Go voice engine remained weeks away.

nodes.label: Current Voice Fidelity Gap
nodes.rationale: Voice is Speaker-only; prompt text is the only knowledge-ceiling control, making voice personas easier to argue past their intended ceiling than text personas.

nodes.label: One Brain Two Parts Visual Model
nodes.source_location: The anatomy; The sync; Who decides what

nodes.label: CandidateSessionAgent
nodes.rationale: Stateless typed-turn adapter: code owns prompt and transcript structure while the model owns reply wording.

nodes.label: Typed Turn Model Round Trip
nodes.rationale: Each reply is generated as a discrete request over the complete transcript rather than a continuous realtime stream.

nodes.label: Text Mode Preamble
nodes.rationale: Preserves fillers and hesitations and constrains the model to one candidate-only text turn.

nodes.label: Voice Session Compiler
nodes.rationale: Compiles one engine contract into provider-native OpenAI Realtime or Gemini Live session documents.

nodes.label: Deterministic Voice Identity
nodes.rationale: Voice is frozen as a persona property so repeated sessions remain comparable.

nodes.label: Hinglish Transcription Hole
nodes.rationale: Code-mixed speech cannot be hinted with a language set; auto-detection is used because pinning either language damages the other.

nodes.label: Prompt-Only Response Pause
nodes.rationale: Neither realtime provider exposes a precise wait-before-answer control, so target pause is advisory prose rather than enforced scheduling.

nodes.label: EngineContract
nodes.rationale: Byte-stable runtime boundary shared by typed sessions, browser voice, and the Go engine.

nodes.label: Dual-Model Runtime Persona Fields
nodes.rationale: Precompiled beliefs, stall phrases, pregate lexicon, unlock spec, and frozen voice carry deterministic persona state into the engine.

nodes.label: Realtime Credential Mint
nodes.rationale: Seals persona instructions into a short-lived provider credential without exposing the prompt to the browser.

nodes.label: Per-Request SQLite Connection
nodes.rationale: A fresh connection and schema initialization per request is explicitly identified as a load bottleneck needing a pool.

nodes.label: No Overload Retry or Backoff
nodes.rationale: Failover handles credential-shaped errors only; it intentionally does not retry 5xx overloads or back off.

nodes.label: Live Session Engine
nodes.rationale: Go runtime intended to perform the interview, with an end-to-end opening-line path working but major production capabilities still incomplete.

nodes.label: Thinker
nodes.rationale: Persona oracle that reasons continuously about what this specific person would say, not what is factually correct.

nodes.label: Claims Ledger
nodes.rationale: Maintains consistent false or limited beliefs across turns instead of allowing random contradictions.

nodes.label: Pre-Synthesized Stall Bank
nodes.rationale: Fills Thinker latency with persona-consistent audio while preserving the frozen voice.

nodes.label: Missing Engine WebRTC Transport
nodes.rationale: WebRTC is still a placeholder, so WebSocket carries all media and lossy networks accumulate latency rather than degrading as bounded glitches.

nodes.label: Missing Engine Transcriber
nodes.rationale: No Transcriber adapter exists; sessions run degraded:asr and end turns from energy detection rather than linguistic evidence.

nodes.label: Missing Engine Recording and Transcript Artifacts
nodes.rationale: The Go engine has no recording, transcript artifact, or S3 upload, preventing its sessions from being graded.

nodes.label: Unwired Runtime Judge
nodes.rationale: Judge adapter exists and is fixture-tested but its verdicts are not connected to the session runtime.

nodes.label: Session Resumption and Context Compression
nodes.rationale: Provider connections last about ten minutes while interviews last 45–60, making reconnection and context compression mandatory.

nodes.label: Silent Audio Turn Failure
nodes.rationale: A provider turn may contain a transcript but produce zero audio; adapter reports silent_turn.

nodes.label: Activity Window Integrity
nodes.rationale: Audio sent outside an activity window disappears without bytes, transcript, or error, so the adapter must open activity on the first frame.

nodes.label: Speaker-Only Browser Voice Limitation
nodes.rationale: Browser voice shares the persona prompt but does not enforce ceiling, false-belief gating, or cross-turn claims consistency outside the model.

nodes.label: No Post-Session Manager Grader
nodes.rationale: Current scorecard is an answer key made at cast time, not an assessment of the manager's actual transcript.

nodes.label: No Session Timeout Sweep
nodes.rationale: Abandoned is present in the schema but never assigned, leaving leaked live sessions without lifecycle cleanup.

nodes.label: RealtimeBroker
nodes.rationale: Mints browser-redeemable credentials but carries no media or model tokens through the control plane.

nodes.label: No Operator Voice Resume
nodes.rationale: Reloading loses the live transport; stored transcript remains, but neither peer connection nor live session handle survives.

nodes.label: No Client-Side Denoising
nodes.rationale: The live path relies on browser echo cancellation, AGC, and optional noise suppression; no RNNoise, gate, or dedicated cleanup stage exists.

nodes.label: Real Audio Automation Gap
nodes.rationale: No automated test exercises the real audio handshake, event mapping, PCM framing, or resumption/goAway behavior.

nodes.label: No Realtime Conversation Telemetry
nodes.rationale: WPM, interruptions, silence handling, and filler density are not extracted from voice sessions.

nodes.label: Gemini Load Rate Limit
nodes.rationale: Flash can return 429 or 503 under burst load; second free-tier keys may share the same capacity problem.

nodes.label: Control Plane Runtime Boundary
nodes.rationale: The control plane owns what the interview is while realtime execution owns how the conversation occurs; no shared runtime interface exists today beyond a planned contract fetch.

nodes.label: Go Engine Handoff
nodes.rationale: README still describes DB/id-based handoff and a start URL as future wiring.
